mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, which reduces discount rates on future corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 6.0% over a 3-month window signals weakening labor market conditions, which increases the likelihood of central bank rate cuts and triggers a flight to equity risk assets, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal fails to outperform a random baseline in 60% of out-of-sample windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in private demand, which increases the probability of monetary policy accommodation and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances, or the interaction term in a multivariate regression has a coefficient with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average, combined with a decline in manufacturing output, signals a contraction in real economic activity, which increases the likelihood of central bank intervention and drives positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal generates negative returns in more than 60% of out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is above 3.0%, the market prices in a high-conviction monetary tightening cycle, which increases the risk of a recession and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal fails to generate negative returns in more than 60% of out-of-sample windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) combined with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong private demand, which increases corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 0.5% MoM and HOUST increases > 1.0% MoM
failure_condition: The joint signal fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a coefficient with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) below 50k per month, combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates labor market slack, which increases the probability of rate cuts and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal fails to outperform a random baseline in 60% of out-of-sample windows.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past quarter, combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO), signals a weakening economy, which increases the likelihood of fiscal or monetary stimulus and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 0% in last quarter AND INDPRO declines > 0.3% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered instances (t-test p > 0.05), or the signal generates negative returns in more than 60% of out-of-sample periods.
